newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican slams U.S. triple executions.
newsitem.headline: Vatican slams U.S. triple executions.

text.p: The Vatican on Thursday condemned a controversial triple execution in the United States, calling it a macabre assembly line of death.
"Capital punishment...means idolising vendetta and relativising the right to life at all costs," the Vatican newspaper L'Osservatore Romano said.
"After the Christmas holidays, the death chambers in American prisons have resumed their sad work and the rhythm seems like that of a macabre assembly line," Vatican Radio said in a commentary.
The executions on Wednesday night in Varner, Arkansas, were only the second triple execution since the United States restored the death penalty in 1976.
The three men were given lethal injections at scheduled intervals in the same execution chamber at the Cummins Unit prison despite a storm of protest from human rights groups.
The last of the three men to be executed, Kirt Wainwright, received a last-minute temporary reprieve when he was already strapped awaiting the injection.
He was then forced to lie there for about an hour while an appeal motion was considered, and finally rejected, by the Supreme Court.

The Roman Catholic Church teaches that the death penalty is legitimate only in the most exceptional circumstances, such as during wars. Pope John Paul has said such circumstances hardly exist in modern times.
There is a growing movement in the Church to support a total ban on capital punishment.
